title: @filter decorator returns empty body {} when combined with serializer_json(auto_unbox=TRUE) in 1.3.3
rationale: Facts: reporter mrcanofcatfood (Plumber 1.3.3, R 4.4.2, Docker/CI) reports GET /health returns HTTP 200 with body {} instead of the expected serialized JSON, when a @filter decorator that mutates res$status/res$body for auth rejections coexists with pr$setSerializer(serializer_json(auto_unbox=TRUE, na='null')) applied globally; switching the same auth logic to plumber::pr_hook(pr, 'preroute', ...) instead of @filter avoids the bug. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a serializer/filter interaction defect, not a usage error, given the isolated pr_hook comparison. Duplicate check: searched 'filter serializer body' in plumber issues; no matching open issue found (only itself and unrelated serializer/parameter issues). Wrong-location check: correct repo -- plumber's own @filter/serializer machinery. Regression check: not applicable -- no comparison to an older plumber release is given; reporter only compares two code paths within 1.3.3. Reproduction plan: needs reprex -- the reporter explicitly states 'We did not narrow this down to a minimal Plumber-only repro,' and the only evidence is two commits in a private, inaccessible repo (unstable-branch/sdm-dashboard); several possibly-unrelated pieces (Postgres pool, custom serializer family, OpenAPI toggle, auth gate) are named as possibly required to trigger it. Impact: moderate if confirmed -- would affect any plumber API combining @filter body mutation with a global JSON serializer, but unconfirmed without isolation. Priority: Medium -- well-documented hypothesis with a working alternative (preroute hook) as a workaround, pending an isolated repro. Recommended next action: label needs reprex and Priority: Medium, and mark ai-triage:done; asking the reporter for a plumber-only minimal reproduction is the correct next step, and this is a routine, non-risky labeling.

title: Templates aren't exercised by CI: 5 chat templates were broken for days
rationale: Facts: maintainer schloerke self-filed this, noting that shinychat 0.7.0 (2026-09-04) made Chat(messages=...) a hard error unless history=False is passed, which broke 5 shiny/templates/chat/** apps (already fixed in #2486, messages= -> greeting=); the underlying problem is that nothing in CI runs the templates -- tests/playwright/examples covers api-examples/ and caught the break immediately (30 red jobs), while templates/ was silent and the breakage was found only by manually grepping for the deprecated call. Proposes a construction-only smoke test per template plus checking how far a no-API-key run gets, and notes two still-red playwright tests and a bundled Agent Skill teaching the same deprecated pattern (also fixed in #2486) as related fallout. Classification hypothesis: bug/test-coverage gap -- not a code regression in py-shiny itself, but a real CI blind spot that let a first-run-breaking defect ship silently. Duplicate check: searched 'template CI test chat'; only itself and an unrelated closed flaky-test epic (#2285) found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- py-shiny owns shiny/templates/** and its own Playwright suite; the triggering shinychat behavior change is already tracked/fixed on the shinychat side. Regression check: not a regression under the rubric's definition (py-shiny's own current behavior lacking coverage, not py-shiny's behavior differing from an older release), so not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: already demonstrated -- 30 red CI jobs plus the five now-fixed template diffs in #2486 serve as the reproduction; the ask here is a smoke test that instantiates each shiny/templates/** app object. Impact: moderate -- the affected surface is literally the first thing a new user runs (shiny create scaffolds), and the gap already caused days of silent breakage; largely mitigated now that #2486 shipped, but the coverage hole remains open. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; a maintainer-scoped, non-controversial test-coverage improvement, safe to label without further review.

title: tool_context() equivalent: per-conversation store and tool-calling context
rationale: Facts: maintainer cpsievert self-filed this, noting that ellmer recently added tool_context() plus a per-conversation chat$store environment (tidyverse/ellmer#1023, part of #871) so tools can access per-conversation state without globals and it survives clone(deep=TRUE); chatlas has no equivalent -- no contextvar-based accessor for the current chat/tool-call context and no per-chat mutable store. Suggests a Python-side tool_context() accessor backed by contextvars.ContextVar set around tool invocation, plus a chat.store dict. A community member (AbarnaaSree) has volunteered to implement it. Classification hypothesis: feature -- parity request mirroring an already-shipped ellmer feature, not a bug. Duplicate check: searched 'tool_context context store'; only itself found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas' own tool-calling/Chat API. Regression check: not applicable -- this capability never existed in chatlas. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a feature request. Impact: low-to-moderate -- a well-defined ergonomics/parity gap for tool authors needing per-conversation state, with a clear implementation template from ellmer and a volunteer already engaged. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored, well-scoped, low-risk feature request with volunteer follow-through already in motion, safe to label without further review.

title: Merge adjacent tool loops when suppressed thinking is the only separator
rationale: Facts: maintainer gadenbuie filed this with a full problem/desired-behavior/acceptance-criteria writeup: show_thinking_after_s can suppress a short thinking block, but the hidden block still splits surrounding tool calls into separate .shiny-chat-tool-loop elements even though CSS already hides the visual gap; equivalent visible transcripts can render with different tool-call groupings depending on whether thinking was suppressed. Proposes coalescing adjacent tool loops when no rendered assistant thinking/content separates them, while keeping loops separate when visible thinking or text intervenes; lists concrete acceptance criteria and required test coverage. Classification hypothesis: feature/UI-consistency issue -- a rendering-grouping inconsistency, not a functional break. Duplicate check: searched 'tool loop thinking group'; only itself and an unrelated closed CSS-renaming issue (#286) found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat's chat-UI tool-loop rendering logic. Regression check: not applicable -- no evidence this grouping ever worked differently in an older shinychat release; it's a gap in the newer show_thinking_after_s suppression feature. Reproduction plan: acceptance criteria already specify the exact scenarios to test; no live repro needed given the maintainer's own root-cause description. Impact: low -- a visual/UX polish issue affecting transcript readability, not data loss or broken functionality. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored, well-scoped UI consistency fix with explicit acceptance criteria, safe to label without further review.

title: History save fails for app-local S7 `Content` subclasses: "Unable to find the S7 class"
rationale: Facts: maintainer gadenbuie filed this with a full standalone R repro: when a Shiny app defines an ellmer::Content subclass in its own R/ files (sourced into an app-local environment, not globalenv()), saving chat history fails with 'Unable to find the S7 class: ContentPromptStyle.' Traces the cause precisely: ellmer::contents_record() serializes non-package classes as a bare name; shinychat's extend_record_linear()/derive_node_ui_from_turns() call ellmer::contents_replay() without .envir, so it defaults to a frame inside shinychat's namespace whose parent chain reaches globalenv() but never the app's local environment; the current workaround (assign(..., envir=globalenv())) works but is non-obvious. Proposes three possible directions. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a precise, reproducible environment-resolution defect in the newer history-save feature. Duplicate check: searched 'S7 class history save'; only itself found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat's chat_server()/history-save code path (R package). Regression check: not applicable -- a gap in code that never handled app-local classes, not a behavior change from an older release. Reproduction plan: the issue includes a complete, directly-runnable standalone R repro that reproduces the exact error message. Impact: moderate -- blocks history-save for any app defining custom Content subclasses outside a package or globalenv(), a pattern natural to typical single-file Shiny apps; a workaround exists but is undocumented. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored with a precise, standalone repro and root-cause analysis, safe to label without further review.

rationale: Facts: community member JamesHWade, building on the in-progress history redesign (#379), asks whether both the Python (chatlas) and planned R (ellmer) history implementations could support workers running without an active Shiny session -- his use case (project 'Deputy') is letting a user select a conversation branch in a Shiny app, continue it in a background R worker via passed user/chat/conversation identifiers, and see the saved continuation when they return; cross-references related design threads (#307 conversation identity, #61 UI-content-vs-model-turns distinction). Classification hypothesis: feature -- a design/scoping question about extending an in-progress feature (#379) to a non-Shiny-session context, not a bug. Duplicate check: not a duplicate of #379/#307/#61 -- those are the related, already-tracked design threads this issue explicitly builds on. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat owns the history feature for both R and Python. Regression check: not applicable. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a design/feature request. Impact: low-to-moderate -- would extend the history redesign's applicability to a legitimate but non-default usage pattern; no user is currently blocked since the base feature is still in development. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; a well-articulated scoping input on in-progress design work, appropriate for the feature owner to fold in at low urgency.

title: Subagent token streams
rationale: Facts: community member wlandau describes building a multi-agent app with ellmer chat objects that call one another as tools (orchestrator -> subagent -> sub-subagent, per tidyverse/ellmer#821), and wants shinychat to expose nested subagent token streams to the user rather than showing only an opaque tool-calling block; includes two runnable R reprexes plus a screenshot showing the current UI where subagent activity is invisible inside the tool-call block. Classification hypothesis: feature -- a well-defined UI/streaming enhancement request, not a bug (the app functions, it just doesn't surface nested-agent output). Duplicate check: searched 'subagent stream'; only itself found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat's chat_ui()/chat_append() rendering owns the tool-call block UI in question. Regression check: not applicable. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a feature request; two complete, runnable reprexes are already included. Impact: low -- a UX enhancement for a specific advanced pattern (nested sub-agent tool calls), not a broadly-blocking gap. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; well-scoped community feature request with runnable reprexes, safe to label without further review.

title: Adjust setView() for each group
rationale: Facts: community member aloboa (2024-09-05) asks whether setView() can be defined per layer group so that selecting a different base/overlay group zooms/pans to that group's own extent, rather than one global initial view; includes a complete runnable R reprex and a screenshot. The issue carried no labels at all until a 2026-09-10 comment from trafficonese pointing to a third-party package, leafem, whose customizeLayersControl(view_settings=..., setviewonselect=TRUE) already implements exactly this per-group-view-on-select behavior. Classification hypothesis: feature -- a capability gap in leaflet's own addLayersControl(), not a bug. Duplicate check: searched 'setView group layer'; no matching open feature request found (results were unrelated bugs). Wrong-location check: correct repo for the feature itself, though a maintained third-party package (leafem) already provides this behavior today. Regression check: not applicable. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a feature request; the reporter's own reprex is complete and runnable. Impact: low -- a real but narrow enhancement request, now with a documented, actively-maintained workaround. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; a two-year-old, previously unlabeled feature request that now has a viable third-party workaround to point the reporter to, safe to close the triage gap without further review.

title: addTiles does not allow display of self-hosted vector tiles
rationale: Facts: community member asitemade4u (2024-03-04) reports that leaflet::addTiles(urlTemplate='.../{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf') against a self-hosted pg_tileserv vector-tile server renders an empty map, while the same endpoint displays correctly via raw Leaflet.js + the Leaflet.VectorGrid plugin; root cause (confirmed by an earlier commenter) is that leaflet R's addTiles()/addProviderTiles() only support raster tile formats, not vector/protobuf tiles. A 2026-09-10 comment points to leaflet.extras2::addVectorgrid() as an existing wrapper that already supports .pbf endpoints. Classification hypothesis: feature -- a missing capability, not a bug in addTiles() itself. Duplicate check: searched 'vector tile' in the leaflet repo and found open issue #279 ('[feature request] Add support for vector tiles', filed 2016, asking for Leaflet.MapboxVectorTile plugin support) -- both #279 and #905 ask for the same underlying capability (vector-tile rendering in leaflet R), making #905 a duplicate of the older, still-open #279. Wrong-location check: correct repo for the feature request itself. Regression check: not applicable. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a feature request; the reporter's own vanilla-JS comparison already isolates the gap. Impact: low -- a real capability gap, now with two independent third-party workarounds identified. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label duplicate (of #279), Priority: Low, and mark ai-triage:done; a clear, high-confidence duplicate of an existing open feature request with a linked rationale, safe to label without further review.

rationale: Facts: community member MatthieuL14 (2021-08-19) asks that addMarkers() support Leaflet's native DivIcon (in place of custom icons), noting that the existing addLabelOnlyMarkers() workaround (suggested on a previously closed issue, #291) does not support click popups, which this request needs. title: Add moving marker functionality
rationale: Facts: community member aljrico (2020-03-08) wants to animate a marker moving continuously along a path (as in the JS Leaflet.MovingMarker plugin), rather than the clunky clearMarkers()+addMarkers() redraw-per-step workaround they demonstrate in a complete runnable Shiny reprex; asks whether this could be added natively or wrapped from the JS plugin. A 2026-09-10 comment points to leaflet.extras2::addMovingMarker() (plus addTimeslider()/addPlayback()) as already-available wrappers providing this functionality. Classification hypothesis: feature -- a plugin-integration/animation-capability request, not a bug (the redraw workaround functions, just inelegantly). Duplicate check: searched 'moving marker'; only itself and an unrelated open plugin request (#443, Leaflet.Deflate) found. Wrong-location check: correct repo for the feature request itself.
